claims.text: The baseline FeCoNiTi-based high-entropy alloy exhibits multiple magnetic or ferromagnetic transitions.
The baseline alloy has suboptimal or excessive hysteresis.
The magnetic transition temperature of the baseline alloy is not precisely aligned with room temperature.
Adjusting the Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti ratios can refine the alloy's phase structure.
Adding a small amount of a complementary element can refine the alloy's phase structure and magnetic anisotropy.
Composition modification alters local magnetic ordering and phase homogeneity.
Altered local magnetic ordering and improved phase homogeneity reduce hysteresis.
Composition modification shifts the magnetic transition temperature toward the desired room-temperature operating regime.
Composition modification changes magnetic anisotropy and stabilizes a phase having a magnetic transition near room temperature.
Decreased phase-boundary scattering and inhomogeneity reduce hysteresis.
Compositional fine-tuning and a minor complementary-element addition will produce a higher magnetic entropy change near room temperature than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy's magnetocaloric response will be more reversible and exhibit less hysteresis than the baseline alloy.
Formation of unwanted secondary phases may prevent the predicted improvement.
A reliably homogeneous microstructure is required for consistent magnetocaloric improvement.
